subject: Request: rolling p50/p95 realignment + regional fallback evidence
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: ops@finserv-ox.com
Cc: k iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Hi team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per FinServ Ox's upcoming cutover (production go-live next month) they've asked for a formal exception path for short-term p95 tolerances in regions during the first two weeks of ramp. I want to capture a clear ask and provide the evidence they need so procurement/legal can sign off.

Quick ask from our side: please share the following by EOD Wednesday so we can assemble the exception package for their security review: 
- Raw percentile computation exports (p50/p95) for the last 90 days, broken out by region and instance type (CSV)
- Rolling-window config (how we compute rolling p95: 10m, 1h, 24h windows) and the code/ops job that publishes the metric
- KV-cache hit rate slices by model variant and sequence-length bucket (png or csv)
- Any transient blackout incidents with timestamps and mitigation steps

Proposed temporary alignment (what we'll ask FinServ Ox to accept):
- Hosted API targets during ramp: p50 60ms, p95 350ms (US region) with a 3-day rolling measurement window for operational alerts, and 1h window for contract measurement.
- Automatic fallback to our dedicated pool or EU region if sustained degradation > 30m is observed.

CC'ing Karthik and Marissa to add technical/contract language.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Operations Team <ops@finserv-ox.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear list. We're especially sensitive to how you define the measurement windows because our regulator wants contract-measured windows to avoid flash penalties. We'll agree to a 1h contract measurement (p95) provided we can see 30/60/90 day history and the breakdowns you requested.

We'll send a point-of-contact for procurement and the SOC reviewer later today. Also, can you confirm whether the fallback to dedicated capacity requires a config change on our end or you handle the routing?

Thanks,
Lina Ortega
Platform Ops, FinServ Ox
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Lina Ortega <ops@finserv-ox.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:40 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Lina / FinServ team —

Short answers:
- Routing/fallback: Redwood handles routing automatically via policy. We'll expose a control to FinServ Ox (console toggle + API) to prefer 'regional-fallback' or 'dedicated-fallback'. No infra change required on their side.
- Measurement windows: We publish three windows in our telemetry: 10m (operational signal), 1h (contract), 24h (trend). Contractually we can tie the SLA to the 1h p95 with a provision for transient carve-outs defined in section 4.2 of the attachment (see doc).

I've attached a prototype CSV export (p95-evidence-2026Q3.csv) with anonymized rows to protect other tenants — it contains timestamp, region, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, p50_ms, p95_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate. I'll follow up with the KV cache graphs tomorrow.

On the proposed temporary targets: Evelyn suggested p50 60ms / p95 350ms. From a telemetry perspective that's reasonable for short bursts on our hosted general-purpose pool for their workload mix (short prompts, mostly chat). If they plan long sequence embeddings at scale, we should tighten expectations.

Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <ops@finserv-ox.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:29:06 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Lina —

I've uploaded the KV cache hit-rate breakdowns and raw computation script to the shared drive (link below). The CSV includes per-request sequence-length buckets (<64, 64-256, 256-1024), and a flag for cache-hit vs origin generation. We also included a short note on how we compute rolling p95 (exponentially weighted percentile with 10m/1h/24h rollups) because we know regulators care about the determinism of computation.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-evidence

Also attaching a short proposal that formalizes the temporary exception path: 14-day ramp window with graduated commitments (day 0-3: p95 target relaxed to 450ms; day 4-7: 400ms; day 8-14: 350ms), with a safety rollback to dedicated capacity if sustained 1h p95 > 600ms. Let us know if procurement wants different cadence.

Marissa
Director, Reliability
From: Lina Ortega <ops@finserv-ox.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finserv-ox.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:15:22 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Marissa / team —

This looks good and the CSVs/graphs are exactly the detail our SOC reviewer wanted. A couple of follow-ups: 
- Can you add an explicit column that shows whether a row was impacted by a fallback event (boolean)? We need to be able to filter incidents tied to failovers.
- For the EU fallback option: we need an estimate of cross-region latency penalty when we failover to EU (we expect a 20-40% increase in p50/p95 due to RTT for our EU users). Do you have measured numbers for that?

Procurement asked whether the graduated cadence could be shortened to 10 days if the early telemetry looks good. Is Redwood open to a 10-day carve-in with the same rollback thresholds?

Thanks,
Lina
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <ops@finserv-ox.com>, Procurement <procurement@finserv-ox.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: latency SLOs — request for rolling-window evidence

Lina / Procurement —

Short answers to your follow-ups: 
- We can add the fallback event boolean to the CSV export and regenerate. Will attach updated file to the drive and link in HubSpot.
- Measured cross-region penalty: for the most common model variant used by FinServ Ox we see median p50 increase ~22% and p95 increase ~28% when routing US->EU (measured over identical request mixes, 7d window). I'll publish the small chart (kv-cache-hitrates-per-region.png) to the drive.
- 10-day carve-in: yes, Redwood is comfortable with a 10-day graduated ramp provided we have daily telemetry and an on-duty Redwood engineer during the window to triage (>95th percentile alerts). We'll include an Ops-runbook and a DocuSign amendment that records the temporary targets and rollback triggers.

Attaching: rolling-window-config-proposal.md (drive) and updated CSV. I'll also create a HubSpot note under deal FSX-2026-0417.

-Ben
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
